title.value: [FICTIONAL] TinyBit: Quantization for Language Model Inference

abstract.value: We propose 4-bit quantization for language model inference. Quantization reduces memory consumption while preserving generation quality on the evaluated tasks. The method targets deployment on a single accelerator.

title.value: [FICTIONAL] DraftRun: Speculative Decoding with a Small Draft Model

abstract.value: Speculative decoding uses a small draft language model and a larger verification model. We report lower decoding latency for short prompts. The draft model proposes tokens which the verification model checks.

title.value: [FICTIONAL] CacheShelf: KV Cache Compression for Long Contexts

abstract.value: We compress the KV cache during language model inference to reduce memory usage for long contexts. A token selection policy retains important cache entries. The authors claim improved memory efficiency.

strengths.value: The quantization approach reduces memory usage. Generation quality appears preserved on the evaluated short tasks.

weaknesses.value: Quantization latency was measured on a single accelerator. Throughput under concurrent requests is not evaluated.
The claim that quantization preserves generation quality is not convincing. The quality evaluation omits long-context tasks, and the comparison lacks a strong quantization baseline.

questions.value: Does quantization preserve quality on long-context generation? Please report uncertainty.

review.value: Speculative decoding latency improves on short prompts. The evaluation omits long prompts and the cost of training the draft model. Acceptance rate varies by workload.

rating.value: 6: weak accept in this fictional scale

summary.value: The paper compresses KV cache memory during long-context inference.

limitations.value: The KV cache compression evaluation lacks retrieval-heavy workloads. Memory savings may depend on context length. Quantization comparisons are absent.

comment.value: AUTHORCOMMENTONLY We will extend the evaluation.
